3º de Primaria · Inglés · Tema 4

Parts of the house

Nombre: ______________________   Fecha: ___________

Qué vas a aprender

  • Name the rooms and parts of a house
  • Name furniture and objects in each room
  • Say where things are with in, on, under and next to
  • Describe your home with there is / there are
  • Name more rooms and say upstairs and downstairs
  • Name things in the kitchen and the bathroom
  • Ask «Is there…? Are there…? How many…?»
  • Talk about housework and homes around the world

Para pensar

Tu gato se ha escondido. Tu amiga inglesa pregunta «Where's the cat?». ¿Cómo le dices que está debajo de la cama, en la cocina?

Explicación

1. House or flat?

We live in different homes. A house (casa) usually has got two floors and sometimes a garden. A flat (piso; in American English, apartment) is a home in a big building with many flats. Some people live in a cottage (casita de campo) or on a farm.

The parts of a building: roof (tejado), wall (pared), door (puerta), window (ventana), chimney (chimenea), stairs (escaleras) and lift (ascensor). ¿Vives en un house o en un flat?

2. The rooms

A home has got different rooms. In the kitchen we cook. In the living room (salón) we watch TV and talk. In the dining room (comedor) we eat. In the bedroom (dormitorio) we sleep. In the bathroom we have a shower and brush our teeth.

Other places: the hall (recibidor), the garage, the garden (jardín), the balcony (balcón) and the attic (desván). Truco: muchas habitaciones acaban en room (habitación): bed + room = dormitorio.

3. Upstairs and downstairs

Many houses have got two floors. To go from one to the other, we use the stairs (escaleras).

  • Downstairs (abajo, en la planta baja), there's usually the hall (recibidor), the kitchen, the living room and sometimes a toilet.
  • Upstairs (arriba), there are usually the bedrooms and the bathroom.

More parts of a home:

  • bathroom (cuarto de baño) and toilet (aseo, váter).
  • garage (garaje): for the car and the bikes.
  • attic (desván): under the roof.
  • basement (sótano): under the ground.
  • balcony (balcón) and terrace (terraza).
  • garden (jardín).

To say where people are, we use in the + room: «Mum is in the kitchen.» «My brother is in the garden.» But we say «Dad is upstairs», without in the.

In the UK, the first floor is the floor above the ground: the ground floor is planta baja, the first floor is primera planta.

Activity: draw a house with two floors and write the names of six rooms.

4. Furniture

Furniture (muebles) is the things we put in the rooms: bed (cama), wardrobe (armario), desk (escritorio), chair (silla), table (mesa), sofa, armchair (sillón), shelf (estantería), lamp (lámpara) and mirror (espejo).

In the kitchen there's a fridge (nevera), a cooker (cocina, fogones) and a sink (fregadero). In the bathroom there's a bath (bañera), a shower (ducha), a toilet (váter) and a washbasin (lavabo). Ojo: furniture nunca lleva -s.

5. In the kitchen and the bathroom

Each room has got its own things. Let's learn the kitchen and the bathroom.

In the kitchen:

  • fridge (nevera): «The milk is in the fridge.»
  • cooker (cocina, fogones) and oven (horno).
  • sink (fregadero): where we wash the dishes.
  • washing machine (lavadora) and dishwasher (lavavajillas).
  • microwave (microondas) and cupboard (armario de cocina).

In the bathroom:

  • bath (bañera) and shower (ducha).
  • washbasin (lavabo) and toilet (váter).
  • mirror (espejo), towel (toalla), soap (jabón), toothbrush (cepillo de dientes).

Be careful with cooker: it is the machine, not the person. The person is a cook! «My dad is a good cook. He uses the cooker every day.»

We can describe what we do in each room: «I have a shower in the bathroom. I have breakfast in the kitchen.»

Activity: make two lists: five things in your kitchen and five things in your bathroom.

6. Where is it? In, on, under

To say where things are, we use prepositions of place. In = dentro de: «The ball is in the box.» On = encima de, sobre: «The book is on the table.» Under = debajo de: «The cat is under the bed.»

En castellano: en español «en» sirve para dentro y para encima («en la caja», «en la mesa»). En inglés hay que elegir: dentro es in y encima es on. Imagina una caja y una pelota para recordarlo.

7. More places: next to, behind, in front of

Other useful prepositions: next to (al lado de): «The lamp is next to the bed.» Behind (detrás de): «The broom is behind the door.» In front of (delante de): «The sofa is in front of the TV.» Between (entre): «The desk is between the bed and the window.»

To ask, say: «Where's my schoolbag?» — «It's next to your desk.» For plurals: «Where are my shoes?» — «They're under the bed.»

8. There is, there are

To describe a room, we use there is (hay, para una cosa) and there are (hay, para varias): «There's a bed in my bedroom. There are two windows.» Negative: «There isn't a TV. There aren't any posters.»

Questions: «Is there a garden?» — «Yes, there is.» / «No, there isn't.» «Are there any stairs?» — «Yes, there are.» En castellano: «hay» es una sola palabra; en inglés depende de si es una cosa (is) o varias (are).

9. Is there…? How many…?

To ask about a room or a house, we put is or are first:

  • «Is there a garden in your house?» – «Yes, there is.» / «No, there isn't.»
  • «Are there any posters in your bedroom?» – «Yes, there are.» / «No, there aren't.»

Remember: in questions and negatives with plurals, we use any: «Are there any books?» «There aren't any chairs.»

To ask about the number of things, use How many…? + plural + are there:

  • «How many bedrooms are there in your house?» – «There are three.»
  • «How many windows are there in the classroom?» – «There are six.»

In the short answers we don't use the short form with yes: we say «Yes, there is», not Yes, there's.

Game: Memory room. Look at a picture of a room for one minute. Then close the book. Your partner asks: «Is there a lamp? How many chairs are there?»

Activity: ask a partner five questions about their home.

10. Reading: Oliver's flat

Read Oliver's email: «Hi! I live in a flat on the fifth floor. It's small but nice. There's a living room with a big sofa and a TV. The kitchen is next to the living room. There are two bedrooms: mine and my parents'. In my bedroom there's a bed, a desk and a wardrobe. My guitar is on the bed and my football is under the desk. There isn't a garden, but there's a balcony with lots of plants. What's your home like?»

Answer: Has Oliver got a garden? Where is his football?

11. My bedroom

Your bedroom is your special place. Describe it: «My bedroom is small and blue. There's a bed next to the window. There are some posters on the wall. My toys are in a big box under the bed. My desk is in front of the window.»

Useful adjectives: big / small, tidy (ordenado) / messy (desordenado), bright (luminoso), cosy (acogedor). ¿Tu habitación es tidy o messy hoy?

12. Homes around the world

People live in very different homes around the world. It depends on the weather, the place and how people live.

  • Igloo: a house made of blocks of ice and snow. Some Inuit people in the Arctic built them for hunting trips.
  • Houseboat: a house on a boat, on a river or a canal. There are many in Amsterdam and London.
  • Stilt house (palafito): a house on long poles over the water or the ground, to stay dry when it rains a lot.
  • Tent and yurt: homes that people can move. Nomads in Mongolia live in round tents called yurts.
  • Cave house: a home inside a hill. In Guadix, in Granada, there are lots of cave houses!
  • Skyscraper (rascacielos): a very tall building with hundreds of flats, like in New York.

And of course, there are castles, farmhouses (masías, cortijos) and caravans.

We can compare them: «An igloo is cold outside but warm inside.» «A houseboat can move.» «There are lots of flats in a skyscraper.»

Activity: choose one of these homes and write three sentences about it with there is or there are.

13. Let's practise: hide and seek

Play Hide the teddy. One pupil goes out of the class. The others hide a teddy bear. When the pupil comes back, he or she asks questions: «Is it under the desk?» — «No, it isn't.» «Is it in the bin?» — «Yes, it is!»

You can also draw a plan of your dream house and describe it: «In my dream house there are ten bedrooms, a swimming pool on the roof and a slide between the floors!» Presenta tu casa soñada a la clase.

14. Helping at home

Everybody in the family can help with the housework (tareas de casa). Here are some jobs that children can do:

  • make my bed (hacer la cama)
  • tidy my room (ordenar mi habitación)
  • lay the table (poner la mesa) and clear the table (quitar la mesa)
  • wash the dishes or load the dishwasher
  • water the plants (regar las plantas)
  • feed the pet (dar de comer a la mascota)
  • take out the rubbish (sacar la basura)
  • sweep the floor (barrer)

To talk about how often we do these jobs, we use words like always (siempre), usually (normalmente), sometimes (a veces) and never (nunca). They go before the verb:

  • «I always make my bed.»
  • «I sometimes lay the table.»
  • «My brother never tidies his room!»

Look: with he and she, the verb takes -s or -es: he makes, she washes, he tidies.

Activity: make a housework chart for your family for one week and tick the jobs you do.

15. My dream house

Now it's time to be an architect (arquitecto)! Imagine your dream house and describe it.

Look at this example:

My dream house is on a beach. It's big and white, and it's got three floors. Downstairs, there's a kitchen with a giant fridge full of ice cream. There's a living room with a slide to the beach! Upstairs, there are five bedrooms and two bathrooms. My bedroom has got a glass ceiling, so I can see the stars from my bed. On the roof, there's a swimming pool. There isn't a garage, because I go everywhere by bike.

To write your description, follow these steps:

  • 1. Where is it? in the mountains, on a beach, in the city, in a tree…
  • 2. What is it like? big, small, modern, old, colourful…
  • 3. What rooms are there? Use there is / there are.
  • 4. What is special? A secret room, a slide, a pool, a tower…
  • 5. What isn't there? Use there isn't / there aren't.

Then draw a plan (plano) or a picture of your house and label the rooms.

Activity: write and draw your dream house and present it to the class.

My home

Ejercicios

  1. Traduce: dormitorio, cocina, baño.

  2. ¿Qué diferencia hay entre house y flat?

  3. Escribe tres muebles del dormitorio.

  4. Completa: «The cat is ___ the bed.» (debajo)

  5. Completa: «The pen is ___ the box.» (dentro)

  6. Completa: «The sofa is ___ ___ the TV.» (delante)

  7. ¿There is o there are? «___ three chairs.»

  8. Pregunta si hay jardín.

  9. ¿Qué hay en el baño? Escribe dos cosas.

  10. Describe tu dormitorio con dos frases.

  11. Where are the bedrooms usually: upstairs or downstairs?

  12. How do you say «nevera» in English?

  13. Answer: Is there a shower in your bathroom?

  14. What's a houseboat?

  15. In the reading, where is the tree house?

  16. Make a question with How many: windows / your classroom.

  17. Translate: hacer la cama, poner la mesa.

  18. Order: never / my brother / tidies / his room.

  19. What's the difference between a cook and a cooker?

  20. Write two things in the bathroom.

  21. Describe the tree house in the reading with three sentences.

  22. Write about a home from another country.

  23. Write your dream house with five sentences.

  24. Make a housework chart and write three sentences with always, sometimes and never.

Practica

  1. We cook in the…

    1. A) bedroom
    2. B) kitchen
    3. C) garage

  2. We sleep in the…

    1. A) bedroom
    2. B) bathroom
    3. C) hall

  3. «Piso» in British English is…

    1. A) floor
    2. B) roof
    3. C) flat

  4. «Nevera» is…

    1. A) cooker
    2. B) sink
    3. C) fridge

  5. The book is ___ the table (encima).

    1. A) on
    2. B) in
    3. C) under

  6. The cat is ___ the bed (debajo).

    1. A) on
    2. B) under
    3. C) in

  7. «Al lado de» is…

    1. A) next to
    2. B) behind
    3. C) between

  8. ___ two windows in my room.

    1. A) There is
    2. B) It is
    3. C) There are

  9. «Is there a garden?» — «No, …»

    1. A) there aren't.
    2. B) there isn't.
    3. C) it isn't there.

  10. «Armario» (ropa) is…

    1. A) window
    2. B) wardrobe
    3. C) wall

  11. «Desván» in English is…

    1. A) basement
    2. B) attic
    3. C) hall

  12. Where do we wash the dishes?

    1. A) in the bath
    2. B) in the fridge
    3. C) in the sink

  13. «___ any posters in your room?»

    1. A) Is there
    2. B) Are there
    3. C) There are

  14. A round tent of the nomads in Mongolia is a…

    1. A) yurt
    2. B) igloo
    3. C) skyscraper

  15. «Poner la mesa» is…

    1. A) make the table
    2. B) do the table
    3. C) lay the table

Explícalo con tus palabras

Incluye: Qué diferencia hay entre house y flat; Cómo se llaman las habitaciones y los muebles; Cómo digo dónde está algo con in, on, under y next to; Cómo describo mi casa con there is y there are.

Tarjetas de repaso

Recórtalas: pregunta delante, respuesta detrás.

house / flatCasa / piso.
kitchenCocina (habitación).
living roomSalón.
bedroom / bathroomDormitorio / baño.
furnitureMuebles (sin -s).
in / on / underDentro / encima / debajo.
next to / behindAl lado de / detrás de.
there is / there areHay (una cosa / varias).
Floorsupstairs, downstairs; attic, basement, garage, hall.
Kitchen and bathroomfridge, cooker, sink; bath, shower, mirror, towel.
QuestionsIs there…? Are there any…? How many… are there?
Homes and houseworkigloo, houseboat, yurt; make my bed, lay the table.

Soluciones

  1. B) Kitchen.
  2. A) Bedroom.
  3. C) Flat.
  4. C) Fridge.
  5. A) On.
  6. B) Under.
  7. A) Next to.
  8. C) Plural.
  9. B) There isn't.
  10. B) Wardrobe.
  11. B) Rooms.
  12. C) Kitchen.
  13. B) Questions.
  14. A) World.
  15. C) Housework.

Soluciones de los ejercicios

  1. bedroom, kitchen, bathroom.
  2. House es una casa; flat es un piso en un edificio.
  3. bed, wardrobe, desk (o lamp, shelf…).
  4. under.
  5. in.
  6. in front of.
  7. There are.
  8. Is there a garden?
  9. a shower and a toilet (o bath, washbasin, mirror).
  10. Model answer: There's a bed next to the window. My books are on the shelf.
  11. Upstairs.
  12. Fridge.
  13. Example: Yes, there is.
  14. A house on a boat.
  15. In a big old oak tree in the garden.
  16. How many windows are there in your classroom?
  17. Make the bed, lay the table.
  18. My brother never tidies his room.
  19. A cook is a person; a cooker is a machine.
  20. Example: a mirror and a towel.
  21. Example: There's a small table. There are cushions on the floor. There isn't a bathroom.
  22. Open answer.
  23. Open answer.
  24. Open answer.
